state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You've made a good observation about Fido falling asleep during the negative-sloping section of the graph. Let's think about what happens when Fido is moving away from home versus when he is at rest. Can you think about how his distance changes in each scenario?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess when Fido is moving away from home, the distance goes up, and when he comes back, it goes down. But I still don't really get how that works with the graph. If he's not moving, wouldn't the line just stay flat instead of going down?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're on the right track with understanding how Fido's distance changes when he's moving versus at rest. Think about what happens to his distance from home when he's not moving but still awake. How might that affect the graph?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks questions requiring reasoning but doesn't directly address the core misconception (confusing rest with movement), and while the student shows some progress in Turn 2 by correctly identifying that flat means not moving, the teacher's Turn 3 response confusingly asks about 'not moving but still awake' which doesn't clarify what the negative slope actually represents (moving toward home).
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to break down the problem and ask guiding questions, they fail to address the student's core misconception about the negative slope representing sleep/rest rather than movement back home, and don't adjust their scaffolding when the student explicitly states confusion in Turn 2.
